boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Pickett's Mill record (May 27, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. Cleburne calls the ground the Pickett Settlement; New Hope Church (GA010) and Dallas (GA011) are separate records. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the IV Corps against Cleburne's Division and Kelly's Brigade without counts; the live field reads zero. Cleburne says he carried 4,683 muskets into the engagement, supported by a dismounted cavalry force on his right and later Quarles's brigade. Cox says Wood's division attacked in a column six lines deep, with Johnson's division (Fourteenth Corps) in echelon and McLean's brigade (Army of the Ohio) as support, and that Wheeler's dismounted cavalry struck Johnson's flank.
claims.rationale: Cleburne's musket count is a partial one-side figure (muskets, not all personnel) for his division; the Union attacking force was not only the IV Corps. No matched count is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Cox says Wood was forced to retire and halted on a ridge in the rear, but calls the ground gained valuable for the extension of the left. Cleburne says Granbury's night charge met no resistance and many Union soldiers fled or surrendered. NPS says the attack was repulsed with high casualties.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Cox's claim that ground was gained is a campaign-level judgment, not the tactical result.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,100 (US 1,600; CS 500); the live field reads 2050 (US 1600; CS 450). Cleburne gives his own loss as 85 killed and 363 wounded, estimates the Union dead at not less than 500 and total killed and wounded at not less than 3,000, and reports 160 prisoners sent to army headquarters besides 72 wounded in his hospital. Cox says Howard reported a total loss of about fifteen hundred, and that Johnston claims seventy wounded and 140 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cleburne's killed and wounded sum to 448 (a computation here), close to the live CS 450; his prisoner figures and Johnston's as quoted by Cox differ. The Union figures are estimates or an approximate total.

open_questions: Howard's, Wood's, Hazen's, Johnson's, Scribner's and McLean's reports, Kelly's and Wheeler's cavalry reports, Hood's corps report (read, not cited here) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Cleburne's May 30, 1864 report, printed within his August 16 report in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
